name: Matbench v0.1 mp_e_form
description: Predict the formation energy of a crystal in eV per atom, as calculated by density functional theory from its crystal structure (Matbench v0.1 task mp_e_form, 132752 samples). The evaluation uses the five official folds: for every fold the candidate is called once, in a separate process, with the other four folds and their target values as training data, and must predict the held-out fold within 600 seconds.

sources.locator: Crystal Graph Convolutional Neural Networks for an Accurate and Interpretable Prediction of Material Properties

Dunn et al. (2020), Benchmarking materials property prediction methods: the Matbench test set and Automatminer reference algorithm (npj Comput Mater): benchmark paper defining the tasks, the nested cross-validation and the metrics; Crossref title verified.
Task table of matbench_v0.1: matbench_mp_e_form: regression/structure, e_form (eV/atom), 132,752 samples..

requirements.datasets: matbench_mp_e_form.json.gz from ml.materialsproject.org, folds from the official validation file

execution.interface: fit_predict(train_inputs, train_targets, test_inputs, info) -> list of len(test_inputs) numbers. Every input is a dict with the keys lattice (the three lattice vectors in angstrom, a 3 x 3 list), species (the element symbol of every site) and frac_coords (the fractional coordinates of every site). info has task, input_type, target, unit, fold, n_train and n_test. Score: mean over the five folds of the held-out mean absolute error, minimized.
notes: matbench_mp_e_form.json.gz from ml.materialsproject.org, folds from the official validation file

limitations: Leaders are graph neural networks and tuned ensembles; the leaderboard snapshot has no date.
Regression MAE averaged over the five official folds.
This task has 106k-133k structures: featurising them is slow, so a candidate must be efficient; the seed uses a cheap feature set.
One evaluation of the starting program took 190 s in the run of 2026-11-11, more than the arena's default limit of 120 s: raise AR_EVAL_TIMEOUT for this task.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Predict the DFT formation energy per atom (eV/atom) of an inorganic crystal from its structure.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Formation energy measures thermodynamic stability and is the first filter for synthesisable compounds, while DFT calculation of every candidate is costly, so a learned predictor widens the space that can be screened.

papers.title: Crystal Graph Convolutional Neural Networks for an Accurate and Interpretable Prediction of Material Properties
papers.task_relation: The paper's targets include the DFT formation energy of Materials Project crystals; the task predicts it on the Matbench subset with free choice of model.
papers.primary_goal: Learn crystal properties directly from the atomic connections of a structure, with a graph neural network trained on Materials Project DFT data (eight properties).
